biography: Craig 'Woodsy' Woods, a name synonymous with controlled aggression on the Australian racing circuit, hails from the dusty plains of Broken Hill. Growing up tinkering with his dad's old Holden ute sparked a lifelong obsession with speed. His raw talent was undeniable, tearing up local dirt tracks before transitioning to tarmac racing in his early twenties. A defining moment came at Bathurst in 2012, where, despite a blown tire, he wrestled his car across the finish line, securing a podium finish against all odds. That grit caught the eye of Reiza Racing, where Woods has remained a loyal, if somewhat controversial, figure. Now in the twilight of his career, Woods is aiming to mentor young drivers while still proving he can mix it with the best. While a championship eludes him, his presence on the grid is always guaranteed to be a spectacle. He is known to still race his dad's Holden ute for charity events.
drivingStyle: Woods' driving style is a blend of controlled aggression and calculated risk. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and fearless corner entries, often pushing his car to the very edge of adhesion. While his tire management isn't always the most conservative, he possesses an uncanny ability to extract maximum performance from his machinery, even when it's on its last legs. Woods thrives under pressure, often delivering his best results when the stakes are highest, a testament to his mental fortitude and unwavering self-belief.
rivalries: Marco Rossi: A clash of generations, with Woods often criticizing Rossi's 'overly cautious' approach to racing.
Isabelle Dubois: An intense rivalry stemming from a controversial collision at Phillip Island, where both drivers blamed each other.
Kenji Nakamura: A battle of egos, fueled by constant on-track battles and off-track taunting. They both believe they are the best driver in the Reiza Racing team.
quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of faded blue racing socks, regardless of the weather.
Before each race, he listens to a specific AC/DC song at full volume to get pumped up.
Insists on personally polishing his helmet visor before every session, even if it's already spotless.
famousQuote: Racing ain't about playing it safe. It's about pushing yourself and your machine to the absolute limit, and then finding a little bit more.
careerHighlight: Winning the Adelaide 500 in 2017, a home race victory that cemented his status as a national hero.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the Bathurst 1000 in 2019, denying him a potential career-defining victory.
